Subject: Follow-up: model fit notes, sample prompts & redaction guidance for DataCo

Hi Emily / Alex —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and a few asks to keep momentum going: 

Summary of what we heard from you:
- Primary use case: automated triage + short-form summarization of clinical intake forms and customer messages (non-diagnostic).
- Volume profile: ~800–1,200 daily requests today, spiking in quarter-end surges; median input length ~350 tokens; 95th percentile ~1,800 tokens.
- Data sensitivity: PII + limited PHI (names, dates, contact info). You need redaction guidance and auditability.

Redwood recommended next steps (we can own these items):
1) Prompt/sample collection: can you share 25–40 representative prompts (actual customer inputs, with PII redacted or replaced) plus 5–10 edge-case examples where the model might hallucinate or misclassify intent? I attached a CSV template (dataco_sample_prompts.csv) — please drop examples there.
2) Model fit & benchmarks: our initial recommendation is to evaluate two tiers: a cost-efficient quantized model for high throughput (rw-7b-instruct-ql8) and a higher-capacity model for complex cases (rw-13b-v2). We’ll run a short eval with your prompts and return token-level latency/cost and quality metrics.
3) Redaction & audit plan: we suggest client-side redaction for obvious PII, plus server-side entity detection and an immutable audit log for review. See the attached discussion notes (tds_dataco_discussion_notes.pdf) for an outline.

Asks for you this week: 
- Upload sample prompts into the attached CSV or paste into a shared doc. Flag any examples that contain PHI you cannot share — we can accept paraphrases.
- Call to schedule a 45-min technical deep-dive (model/ops) next week — are you available Tue/Wed afternoon PST?

We’ll queue an internal eval plan once we have your samples. I’ve looped in Karthik (product) for deployment constraints and Marissa (ML) for model/eval design.

Thanks —
Priya Natarajan

Priya —

Appreciate the clear recap. I attached a quick export of 12 representative prompts (we redacted direct identifiers) and added 3 edge-case notes inline below. We’ll try to get the full CSV into your template by Monday.

Samples (inline, paraphrased):
1) "Patient reports ongoing cough and recent travel — summarize key intake points and flag for follow-up."
2) "Customer message: I'm allergic to penicillin, need an alternative — prioritize and route to pharmacy team."
3) "Free text: patient gave two phone numbers and a personal email — collate contact info."

Edge cases we worry about:
- Ambiguous negation ("no history of diabetes" vs. "no history recorded").
- Long concatenated forms where forms were OCR'd with artifacts.
- Sensitive notes that include family history (we want to avoid any PHI leakage in summaries).

Redaction note: our legal/privacy team is uncomfortable sharing raw PHI even in paraphrased form; we prefer either (A) a redaction pipeline that strips names and contact before sample export, or (B) we can provide synthetic paraphrases. What do you recommend? Also curious on which of the two model options you suggested tends to overfit to formatting artifacts.

Thanks Priya — reviewed the samples Emily sent. High level recommendations before the deep-dive: 

Model recommendations (to benchmark):
- rw-7b-instruct-ql8 (quantized) — good baseline for throughput and cost-conscious routing. Expect ~12–18ms per token on a single A100-class GPU with Redwood batching; strong when prompts are short to medium. Might be brittle on messy OCR artifacts without prompt normalization.
- rw-13b-v2 — higher capacity for longer contexts (helps with the 95th percentile ~1,800-token cases) and better on negation/long-range coreference. Latency ~25–35ms/token; higher per-token cost but fewer quality regressions.

Eval plan (deliverable):
- 12 core prompts (paraphrased/synthetic accepted) + 5 edge-case prompts.
- Metrics: ROUGE/QA-pair accuracy (where we have labels), hallucination rate (manual review), latency percentiles, token cost estimate.
- Acceptance threshold: >92% intent classification accuracy on triage labels; hallucination <3% on summaries.

Redaction approach:
- Client-side: recommend DataCo strip direct identifiers (names, phone, SSN-like) before sending. We can provide a redaction regex bundle and a small local helper library.
- Server-side: run a lightweight NER + pattern detector in the Redwood pipeline (we can hash/redact sensitive spans and write the original token offsets to an immutable audit record for compliance).
- For PHI that is disallowed from leaving their environment, we can run the model in Private mode (VPC) or provide a semi-synthetic prompt pathway — we should surface Private options in the proposal.

Prompt engineering notes:
- Add a short system instruction for formatting (bullet list of extracted items) and a "do not invent" clause.
- Normalize OCR artifacts (strip repeated punctuation, run basic whitespace normalization) before model input.

Attachments I’m sharing: redaction_guidelines_v1.docx (contains regex examples, sample pseudocode for client-side redactor), and a link to an internal benchmark for a small pilot: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/dataco-eval-2026.

Next steps I can own: draft the 12+5 eval pack and run a quick 2-day A/B between rw-7b-instruct-ql8 and rw-13b-v2 once DataCo uploads samples. Priya — I'll add a short slide with expected latency/cost tradeoffs for the deep-dive.

Marissa Cole
